scope: Paired SIMLOX 2017 CLI comparison of a larger CALHOURS PM with and without PMRID=CAL24 on the accepted D05 two-aircraft shared-worker model. Check whether starting the larger PM cancels or resets the smaller PM due immediately afterward, including task and resource ledgers.

dependency.accepted_behavior: One critical five-hour repair books the sole P-MAINT worker 23-28; the two existing one-hour CAL24 PMs work 28-29 and 29-30, with event and half-hour resource-ledger acceptance.

manual.rule: MaterielPM.PMRID identifies a more frequent smaller PM included in the current PM. Initiating the current PM cancels the related task and resets its counters; no formal interval restriction. ENREG=Y retains original calendar schedule despite delays.

frozen_source_delta: D05 Control SIMPE/RCEND and both MISSION/SYSTEM ResultCollection.RCEND values 36->60 hours; ProblemDescription names each arm.
Existing CAL24 MaterielPM ENREG null->Y so the second calendar due remains hour 48 after first due at 24, even though worker contention delays work to 28-30.
Add BIG47 system PM with CALHOURS interval 47, ATIM=DTIM=0 and one-hour INSPECT subtask requiring the same sole P-MAINT worker at BASE-01.
The linked and unlinked arms differ only in BIG47.PMRID CAL24 versus null, aside from descriptive text; both retain D05 repair/failure/mission/worker parameters.
acceptance_hypotheses: Both arms share an identical event trace before the BIG47 due at hour 47, including one five-hour critical repair, two first-cycle CAL24 work episodes and three original missions. The new PM and longer horizon may change the exact earlier failure draw compared with D05; measure actual timing rather than assuming parent random-stream parity.

The BIG47 due at hour 47 starts before the CAL24 second calendar due at hour 48. In the unlinked control, any second-cycle CAL24 work is independently scheduled. In the linked arm, initiation of BIG47 cancels/resets its related CAL24 work so the first post-47 small PM differs observably. Exact event ordering and the impact of the one-worker queue must be established from native logs.

Native import/export retains all authored populated cells, both converter summaries show zero errors and usable SXOs, and the two 120-bin System/Resource/Stock ledgers reconcile with event work/worker booking and terminal state.
gate: Accept only the observed pairwise PMRID effect after exact source diff, zero converter errors, valid simulation output, individual task starts/completions/cancellations, resource capacity and report-bin reconciliation, and separate read-only replay. If the hypothesis fails, retain the immutable run as a diagnostic and revise a new version; do not publish a PMRID generalization.
execution_guard: Session-0 SSH with sshd ancestor, Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue, GUI PID 13340/session 1 active and identity-preserved, immutable run path, 60-second targeted child watchdog, source/tool hashes before/after and raw SHA-256 closure.
limits: One two-aircraft system, one seed, one base and one shared worker; no generic scheduling, multi-level PMRID, remote-base PM, ENFNC, stochastic PM or GUI/cross-engine claim.
D12.var01 started-small-PM interruption may require a separate arm if this pair only establishes the not-yet-started branch; full D12 remains open.
